articleTitle: Application of Simple Linear Phase Recursive Bandpass Filters for the Extraction of Electroencephalogram Waves
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: A simple type of recursive digital bandpass filters with linear phase characteristics is reconsidered, suitable when using limited computing resources such as in low-cost portable digital signal processing (PDS) applications. The extraction of the low frequency rhythms of an electroencephalogram (EEG) signal serves as a guide to illustrate the advantages of operation of this type of filters, as well as a didactic resource in the teaching of PDS in Bioengineering.

articleTitle: Modeling the Laser Flash Method for Thermal Characterization of Fat Tissue Mimicking Phantom
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This paper describes a computational implementation of the laser flash method to determine the thermal conductivity of fat tissue in the software COMSOL Multiphysics, the simulated laser generates a transient temperature rise. By measuring the time that it takes for the heat to be distributed throughout the material, the thermal diffusivity coefficient can be determined, and the thermal conductivity can be calculated. This is important for predicting the heating effects in hyperthermia treatments where heat absorption and dissipation in adipose tissues are involved. The design of a 2D geometry simplifies the computational load by reducing the model's complexity. It also enables the implementation of boundary conditions that simulate the heat source as a Gaussian laser beam and the thermal insulation to emulate an adiabatic environment. As a result, the time it took to reach half of the maximum temperature was 1.416 s, which differs from the theoretical value. Considering the absorption coefficient (µa) in the model with a thermal conductivity of 0.21 W m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>K-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, the error decreases from 5.34 % to 0.162 %. Despite this, the model presents a methodology for the thermal characterization of a phantom composed of adipose tissue in the absence of a thermal analyzer.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Conventionally Focused and Non-Diffracting Frozen Waves in Diffractive Environments for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis based on simulations of three acoustic focalization techniques employed in biomedical ultrasound: annular phased array, concave transducer, and non-diffracting “Frozen Waves.” The Frozen Waves technique, noted for its self-reconstruction capabilities, is evaluated for its consistency in acoustic field profile, even in diffractive environments. The analysis employs two simulation models: one in a homogeneous water medium and another incorporating a bone-like obstacle. In the homogeneous medium, the results were consistent with the defined parameters. When a bone-like obstacle was introduced, Frozen Waves demonstrated stable focalization, exhibiting less pressure attenuation and energy reflection. In contrast, both the annular phased array and concave transducer methods showed increased wavefront distortion and significant pressure accumulation at the obstacle site, with pressure increases of 155.26% and 163.16%, compared to the focal point pressure in the homogeneous model, respectively. These results highlight the resilience of Frozen Waves to diffraction and attenuation in complex environments, positioning them as a promising technique for enhancing the efficacy and safety of ultrasound-based medical procedures.

articleTitle: GoogleNet-Based Classification System for Knee Osteoarthritis Detection in Radiographic Images
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease significantly impacting quality of life, particularly among older populations. This paper presents a sophisticated deep learning-based approach for identifying and categorizing knee OA. Radiographic images were processed with Faster R-CNN for precise localization of pathological features and GoogleNet for classification into four grades of severity. A dataset of 1650 manually annotated grayscale X-rays was used, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 91.9%, with grade-specific accuracies as follows: Grade 1 (90.57%), Grade 2 (90.63%), Grade 3 (93.71%), and Grade 4 (96.11%). The model exhibited high sensitivity across all grades, reaching 93.7% for Grade 3, and specificity values remained strong, peaking at 99.3% for Grade 4. Error rates ranged from 3.89% to 9.43%, while F1 scores demonstrated reliable performance, averaging above 91%. This automated method improves efficiency and lowers diagnostic subjectivity, particularly in advanced cases where the model showed its highest performance. The system's capacity to reduce diagnostic workloads and facilitate individualized treatment plans is highlighted by its telemedicine adaptability and clinical environment scalability. To improve musculoskeletal illness management and increase reliability in real-world applications, future improvements will concentrate on increasing classification accuracy for intermediate grades.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Stimulation as an Inhibitor for Cell Viability In Vitro on a MDA-MB-231 Cell Model.
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The effects of extremely low-frequency electromagnetic fields (ELF-EMF) exposure and its classification related to human health remains as a subject matter that has not yet been fully explored and investigated. A possible therapeutic role for this type of radiation is suggested under specific parameters combination of frequency, intensity and exposure time leading to new strategies for major diseases treatment. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of variations in extremely low frequency electromagnetic fields´ frequency and intensity on an in vitro model of triple negative breast cancer (TNBC).

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Supervised Segmentation of Infrared Foot Sole Images Based on a Bayesian Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) continues to be a significant challenge for public health, with a considerable impact on global mortality rates. One of its most severe complications is diabetic foot syndrome, which, without proper treatment, can lead to ulceration and amputations. In this context, medical thermography offers a non-invasive approach to detecting thermal abnormalities in the skin, positioning it as a promising tool for the early detection of these complications. This paper presents a segmentation algorithm applied to thermographic images of the plantar region, developed using a Bayesian classification model. This model uses color features from the images to effectively segment the plantar region achieving a sensitivity of 0.7574. However, increasing the color samples could further enhance the model especially by variations in image acquisition conditions (e.g., lighting, sensor calibration). Future work will focus on expanding the dataset, adaptive color sampling, and alternative feature extraction methods to enhance robustness and segmentation sensitivity.

articleTitle: Thermal dose Analysis for High Intensity Focused Ultrasound Applications in Continuous and Pulsed Mode
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Thermal ablation is a method used to cause tumor cell death by heating the tissue, and one way to achieve this is to use the heating properties of ultrasound with High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU). Thermal ablation with HIFU has been shown to be a noninvasive and effective approach to tumor treatment. There are different approaches to the application of HIFU, two of which are continuous and pulsed. To characterize these two modalities, a comparative analysis of the thermal dose (TD) achieved by continuous and pulsed HIFU is performed, keeping all the other parameters constant. The thermal dose is calculated from the temperatures measured using thermocouples inserted in ex vivo skeletal muscle tissue (SMT) samples, exposed to both modalities. A single element HIFU transducer with a f = 1.1 MHz (Sonic Concepts H-104 Transducer Series, Ø64 mm, WA, USA) is used to generate the ultrasound pulses. The continuous mode used consists of a single pulse of 20 s of duration; whereas the pulsed mode consists of two pulses of 10 s of duration separated by 5 s of dead time, during which there is no sonification. Both are excited with an input of 350 mV, resulting in an output power of 31 ± 1 W, this way the same amount of energy is deposited in the sample by both modalities. The TD model CEM43 was used to analyze the response of the sample to the continuous and pulsed HIFU, which is one of the most widely accepted for thermal dosimetry. The results show that the use of continuous HIFU achieves slightly higher temperatures than pulsed HIFU, but the difference becomes more notable in the calculated TD, being the dose of continuous HIFU several times the dose of pulsed HIFU.

articleTitle: Differential Hemodynamic Responses in Cortex to Horizontal Visual Scanning Measured with fNIRS
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The visual system enables us to perceive our environment and perform functions such as safe navigation. An example of a critical component of effective perception is gaze stability, which relies on the vestibular system. The vestibular system is also essential for the perception and control of self-movement. This study explores the behavior of cortical areas associated with these systems, examining differences in hemodynamic responses under conditions when visual attention is present versus when is absent, using fNIRS to assess brain activity. The experiment involved 19 participants, allowing for a clear distinction between these two conditions. The results revealed specific cortical areas exhibiting different patterns of activity during task performance.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Discriminative Power of Cardiovascular and PPG-Derived Biomarkers for Blood Pressure Classification: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Hypertension is a major global health concern and a leading risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, stroke, and kidney failure. Accurate and continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring is crucial for early detection and effective management of hypertension-related conditions. Traditional cuff-based BP measurement methods, although widely used in clinical settings, are impractical for continuous tracking due to their intermittent nature and potential discomfort. Consequently, there is growing interest in developing non-invasive, cuffless BP monitoring techniques that rely on physiological signals such as photoplethysmography (PPG) and other cardiovascular biomarkers. In this context, identifying reliable markers that can accurately classify BP levels is essential for advancing cuffless monitoring technologies. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of selected cardiovascular and PPG-derived biomarkers in distinguishing normal from abnormal BP, following a structured approach that includes signal preprocessing, feature extraction, and machine learning-based classification.

articleTitle: Multiview Deep Neural Networks for Tumor Classification in Breast Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This study proposes a multiview convolutional neural network (CNN) for tumor classification in breast images. This CNN architecture receives multiple images simultaneously, specifically from three tumor regions of interest: internal, which contains only the tumor region; middle, which contains the transition zone between the tumor and the adjacent tissue; and external, which contains the peritumoral region. The multiview CNN was evaluated on mammography and breast ultrasound images and compared against a traditional single-view CNN. The multiview CNN achieves an AUC of 0.950 for mammograms, while the single-view CNN reaches 0.923. Likewise, the multiview CNN obtains an AUC of 0.936 for breast ultrasound, while its single-view counterpart attains 0.883. These results demonstrate the superiority of multiview CNNs in both imaging modalities because they obtain complementary information from several tumor regions of interest where radiologists usually focus their attention.

articleTitle: Test Chamber for PM Monitoring Devices with a Python-Based GUI and Control System Using Wireless Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Particulate matter (PM) is one of the most dangerous air pollutants which consists of particles containing microscopic solid or liquid droplets of various sizes and shapes of different chemicals [1], [2]. These particles are usually divided into two basic particle metrics, PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> (aerodynamic diameter ≤ 10 micrometers) and PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> (aerodynamic diameter ≤ 2.5 micrometers) and is directly associated with the potential to cause health problems in people who are exposed [1], [3], [4]. PM can cause problems such as eye, nose and throat irritation, impact the central nervous system, cause obstructive pulmonary disease, impact the reproductive system, develop cardiovascular problems and develop lung cancer [5], [6]. The health impact produced by air pollutants has generated a trend in the design and manufacture of portable, personal and fixed PM monitoring systems to prevent exposure to air pollutants. However, these devices still need to address some issues, such as calibration, which is expensive and often takes a long time to perform, and some PM sensors need to be properly evaluated to compete with environmental monitors on the market. In this work, a portable test chamber with controlled environmental conditions and a wireless connectivity, to avoid exposure to PM, has been developed for the calibration and evaluation of low cost portable and personal PM sensors. The dimensions of the test chamber are: 66cm base, 39cm height and 33cm depth. To interface with air monitoring devices, environmental sensors and control tools (e.g., fans, motors, air extraction devices, etc.) an air quality monitoring control software Python-based with a graphical user interface (GUI) was developed using an Arduino Uno in each device to communicate via Bluetooth using a HC-06 device, while the pDR-1500 particle monitoring devices were interfaced and communicated via Wi-Fi (2.4GHz or 5GHz) using a Raspberry Pi 5 for each device. Two tests of 100 PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> measurements were performed, taking measurements every three seconds for 5 minutes, using incense as the source of pollution, of which the first test was between two calibrated pDR-1500 particle monitoring devices, while the second test was between a calibrated and an uncalibrated pDR-1500 particle monitoring device. During the tests, the relative humidity ranged from 33 to 35%, which indicates that the majority of the PM inside the test chamber was not affected by humidity, as mentioned in the work of [7]. In these tests, Pearson correlation analysis (r) was performed, which resulted with an r of 0.9947 in the first test between the calibrated devices, and an r of 0.9698 in the second test between the calibrated and non-calibrated devices. Moreover, a test was performed to corroborate the robustness of the performance and data transfer in which records were taken for 24 hours (1 sample per second), resulting in an average of 99.98% of successfully measured data for the GY-39 sensor and 100% for the pDR-1500 devices. This work contributes to the problems associated with personal and portable PM monitors by addressing the costly and time-consuming calibration process of commercial monitors. Furthermore, with the increasing demand for the development of new portable or low-cost PM sensors, it contributes to the validation and evaluation of these new devices. Another advantage of our prototype is the elimination of the risk of user exposure to PM during testing thanks to its wireless connectivity. For future work, adapting the test chamber to monitor other gases such as ozone (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), etc., is considered. Additionally, test with particles of known size and monodisperser will be used to introduce only particles of a specific size to increase the stringency of the process and prevent contamination with other particles.

articleTitle: Comparison of a High-Precision and a Low-Cost VNA for Breast Cancer Ablation Studies
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This paper highlights the growing importance of developing alternative methods to mastectomy surgeries, given the increasing incidence of breast cancer in young women. One such alternative is microwave ablation, a minimally invasive technique. This study compares two vector network analyzers (VNAs): the high-precision Agilent E5071B and the low-cost NanoVNA V2 Plus4. Tests were conducted using various materials at different times of the day, revealing a strong correlation between results, with a mean squared error of less than 1%. Accurate measurement of S11 parameters and permittivity is crucial for designing antennas intended for breast cancer ablation, ensuring efficient energy delivery to the targeted tissue.

articleTitle: Estudio de Factibilidad para la Aplicación de la Técnica de Ablación por Microondas a Tejido Ex-Vivo de Mastectomías: A study to see if using microwave energy to remove tissue in mastectomy surgeries is a good idea.
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: El cáncer de mama es el cáncer más común y mortal entre las mujeres de todo el mundo. El procedimiento de eliminación de tejido mediante microondas (MWA, por su acrónimo en inglés), es una terapia mínimamente invasiva que utiliza radiación electromagnética para destruir las células tumorales. El tratamiento de ablación por microondas es una técnica innovadora para el tratamiento de pacientes que presentan alguna comorbilidad o que no quieren ser operados por así ser su decisión. Este estudio tiene como objetivo evaluar la factibilidad y los resultados preliminares de esta técnica en el entorno hospitalario mediante un convenio de colaboración.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Development of a Medium-Power Ultrasonic Generator for Bone Consolidation Therapy
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Ultrasound (UT) has numerous medical applications, including therapeutic, surgical, and diagnostic procedures. The emission of medium-intensity ultrasound is crucial for the rapid recovery of patients with bone consolidation deficiencies, as it promotes faster healing, reduces the need for surgical interventions, and lowers associated hospital costs. This article presents the design, simulation, and development of a medium-power ultrasonic generator for therapeutic purposes. The design process, development stages, and results are detailed, highlighting the implementation of therapeutic medical equipment developed as part of the project milestones for Ultrasonic Systems for Biological Tissue Therapy (SUTBIO), initiated in 2024.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Clustering on Breast Cancer Cell Culture Images
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Usage of images as sources of information in assays requires a degree of image processing, which can be performed by a hu man observer in the quality of a subjective estimation,or performed by amethod which leverages the intensity values that make up the image and ultimately represent an objective measurement,resulting in the ability to conclude statisticallywhether there is or not a certain characteristic intrinsic to the image. In this work,the application of k-Means is evaluated within an unexplored whole-cell culture perspective to provide new insights on potential large-scale signaling processes.

articleTitle: Development of a AD8233-Based EMG Sensor and Double Interrupt Sampling Technique in a Low-Cost Prototype for Biosignal Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: According to the World Health Organization, mental disorders have important repercussions in people's health, monitoring physiological parameters on patients becomes useful to identify mental disorders, but these devices are often expensive, which limits their availability to educational and research institutions. In this work, a low-cost equipment for the acquisition of biosignals such as body temperature (BT), electrocardiograph (ECG), electromyogram (EMG), galvanic skin resistance (GSR), heart rate (HR), oxygen saturation level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$( {\text{Sp}{\mathrm{O}_2}} )$</tex> and a sensor based on the AD8233 integrated circuit for the acquisition of EMG was developed applying the Nyquist theorem. Furthermore, a new sampling method is employed in which two software interrupts at different frequencies are used with the ATmega2560 microcontroller allowing the sample of multiple signals at the same time. This work demonstrated that the development of an electromyogram sensor based on the AD8233 integrated circuit provides a full electromyogram signal. Furthermore, the developed prototype with an Arduino Me ga board can acquire 6 biosignals simultaneously using two sampling frequencies on test over 6 hours, operating at a fixed 1 Hz for BT, GSR, HR and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Sp}{\mathrm{O}_2}$</tex> while at the same time ECG and EMG signals are acquired at 500 Hz, 625 Hz or 800 Hz.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Electroporated Volume in Skeletal Muscle of a Murine Model for the Transfection Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: In vivo electrotransfection (ECT) increases the efficiency of plasmid DNA incorporation into myocytes, ECT enables the stable integration of DNA into the cell genome, allowing for the temporary expression of proteins. In this study, an approach to real anatomical modeling is presented, necessary to plan a highly efficient and safe process for the animal model used. The distribution of the electric field, in a volume corresponding to the skeletal muscle to be transfected, is analyzed by applying electric potentials varying between 80 V and 130 V through two plate electrodes. The results obtained by the Finite Element Method (FEM) analysis suggest that, for skeletal muscle in the murine model, the electric potential applied between the electrodes should not exceed 105 V, to avoid significant tissue damage and control the specific transfection regions.

articleTitle: Image Processing Software to Quantify Cell Migration During Wound Healing Assay in Cancer Research
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: For this project, in the need of a standardized method to process and analyze images obtained from a technique to evaluate cell migration during cancer research, an image processing software was developed using MATLAB. This program automatically identifies the area of a wound in a cell culture and calculates the number of pixels in it to quantify cell migration. The software delivers accurate and precise results to support cancer investigations, 17 times faster than manual methods with an accuracy of 2.8%.

articleTitle: A Novel Curriculum Sampling Method for Hard Observations Classification in Breast Cancer Ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common neoplastic disease among women, with over 2.3 million diagnoses and 685,000 deaths recorded globally in 2020. In Brazil, it is estimated that 73,610 cases will be diagnosed between 2023 and 2025, corresponding to 66.54 new cases per 100,000 women. However, the prognosis tends to be favourable if treated early. Thus, it is essential to diagnose the disease in its early stages. Ultrasound imaging helps distinguish between cystic and solid masses and determine tumour malignancy. A Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) system that employs deep learning methods can serve as a second opinion for specialists, increasing the accuracy of evaluations. However, there are a few challenging cases in which the ultrasonographer makes a mistake. Thus, this work proposes a novel Curriculum Learning (CL) approach that focuses on hard cases to reduce the number of false positives and false negatives on a breast ultrasound dataset. Our proposed Adaptive Sampling approach achieves an Accuracy of 86.14 ± 3.02, a Sensitivity of 86.46 ± 2.84, a Specificity of 85.99 ± 4.00 and a F1-Score of 80.26 ± 3.67.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Automatic Pointer Based on Eye Movement Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The Tobii Eye Tracker 5 is an advanced eye tracking device that accurately captures the user's eye movements. This equipment is used in the control interface, allowing the person to select options by eye gaze, such as directions to follow or commands to execute. The development of the control system has been programmed in Python. The pointer was programmed to perform an automatic click after 3 seconds of eye fixation on a point. To optimize accuracy, a conversion of the pointer position from pixels to centimeters was implemented so that, within a radius of 2 cm around the target, the system executes the click. This adaptation was designed considering that eye tracking may present slight fluctuations, and the established margin of error ensures that the interaction is performed without the need for perfect eye fixation. This automatic click system enhances control of both the interface and device functions, without requiring exact eye coordination. This is especially beneficial for users with limited mobility or motor disabilities.

articleTitle: Modeling the Ultrasound-Induced Heating in Bone and External Layers
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Bone consolidation is a process of cellular differentiation regulated by a series of growth factors and cytokines, where bone heating plays a role although this heating effect is subtle, it is biologically significant since it activates various mechanisms for bone healing. To perform a preliminary temperature estimation, a simulation combining acoustic equations and bioheat equations was performed to study the thermal response in a time-lapse study. In this study, we solved both the acoustic equation and the bioheat equation related to this physical phenomenon in order to simulate the thermal echo in the bone as well as its surrounding tissues such as muscle and skin. An acoustic source frequency of 1 MHz was chosen.

articleTitle: Analysis of Generative Patterns in Image Generation with Autoencoders and BigGAN: Applications in Osteosarcoma
publicationTitle: 2025 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/ Pan American Health Care Exchanges (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The generation of synthetic medical images offers solutions to challenges such as limited datasets and ethical constraints in healthcare research. This work evaluates two deep learning models-Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)-for generating and reconstructing histological images of osteosarcoma. A dataset of 1144 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained images annotated as viable tumor, necrotic tumor, and non-tumor was used to train and assess both architectures under comparable conditions. The VAE achieved a steady reconstruction loss reduction from 0.15 to 0.04 over 175 epochs. Reconstructed images reached a mean Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.552 and a mean Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.012, effectively preserving structural features but partially losing finer textures. Meanwhile, the BigGAN was trained for 2000 epochs, achieving a peak SSIM of 0.739 and a corresponding MSE of 38.28 during early epochs, demonstrating its capacity to generate highly detailed synthetic images with significant variability. These results underscore the complementary strengths of both models: the VAE's robust latent representation ensures reliable reconstructions, while the BigGAN excels in producing high-quality synthetic images. Combining these approaches has potential to augment histopathological datasets, advancing diagnostic algorithms and computational pathology.
